name: Harshdeep Hortico Ltd
tagline: Rs ~130 Cr BSE-SME micro-cap in premium pots, planters and garden decor - FY26 revenue +22% to Rs 69 Cr, PAT +29%, ROE ~23%, EBITDA margin ~29%, and cheap at ~10x earnings; the persistent constraint is cash conversion - FY26 operating cash flow was negative even before capex as working capital and inventory absorbed cash
business_overview: Harshdeep Hortico (BSE-SME listed Feb 2024) manufactures and markets premium pots and planters, decorative planters, garden accessories, shade nets and outdoor furniture, plus newer verticals 'Agri Shield' (technical agro shade nets), 'Muebles' (furniture) and India's first rotomoulded decorative water fountains (launched Apr 2026). It sells to nurseries, garden centres, landscapers, architects and institutional buyers - airports (Mumbai, Mangalore), hotels, builders and infrastructure projects - where execution and reliability matter more than price.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 130 Cr (BSE SME); ~10x FY26 P/E, ~6.5x EV/EBITDA, ~2.2x P/B
FY26 revenue Rs 68.7 Cr (+22% YoY), PAT Rs 12.5 Cr (+29%), PBT Rs 16.0 Cr (+41%), EBITDA Rs 19.8 Cr (~29% margin, +32%); H1 FY26 PAT +35%, H2 FY26 decelerated to revenue +15% / PAT +25%
Near debt-free but FY26 added ~Rs 3.8 Cr secured loans; FY26 operating cash flow NEGATIVE Rs 8.4 Cr (working-capital + inventory build) BEFORE capex of Rs 8.5 Cr - deeply negative FCF

Second dividend (Rs 0.25/sh FY26) while expanding; net worth Rs 59.9 Cr (+44%); new lines - shade nets 3.5 lakh kg/yr, Agri Shield +200 t, total moulding capacity 1,440 t/yr, rotomoulded fountains, Muebles furniture; promoter family retains a large stake
fundamentals_narrative: For a micro-cap the return profile is strong - FY26 ROE 23.3%, ROCE ~24%, EBITDA margin ~29% - and growth is real and broad-based (FY26 revenue +22%, PAT +29%), driven by new categories (outdoor furniture, shade nets, Agri Shield, rotomoulded fountains), exports and distribution expansion. Two things the FY26 filing sharpened: (1) growth decelerated through the year - H1 revenue was up ~31-35% but H2 only +15% - and (2) cash conversion is not just a capex story: FY26 operating cash flow itself was negative Rs 8.4 Cr as inventory and working capital absorbed cash, and the company drew ~Rs 3.8 Cr of new secured loans to fund the shortfall plus Rs 8.5 Cr of capacity capex. The claimed moat is a combination rather than a single dominant one - 500+ designs and 2,200+ SKUs on a mould library built over years, a nationwide dealer/nursery/landscaper network, and institutional relationships (Mumbai and Mangalore airports) that take time to earn - but the underlying moulded-plastic products have low manufacturing barriers, so the ~29% EBITDA margin carries some normalisation risk. Offsetting all of this, the stock trades at ~10x FY26 earnings and ~6.5x EV/EBITDA, which prices in almost no growth.
technical_read: Not independently pulled; thinly-traded BSE-SME name, so price action is illiquid and volatile. Stock reportedly fell after the strong FY26 print, on the growth deceleration and negative operating cash flow.
sentiment_summary: Small 5-post thread (since Jul 2026). abhicnr (elevated) authored a well-received intro (7 loves): Rs 130 Cr mcap, ~Rs 69 Cr revenue, ~Rs 13 Cr PAT, ROE ~23%, D/E ~0.06, 3-yr CAGR ~25%, moat from the design/SKU/mould library plus distribution and institutional relationships. The only substantive pushback (RoyD) is that cash flows are getting locked in working capital, FCF is negative, and scaling a low-barrier plastic-products business will be a challenge; abhicnr's reply frames the working-capital drag as a normal early-growth investment phase, noting the company still declared its first dividend. The FY26 filing broadly validates the bear's cash-flow concern.

thesis_fit: 10x-in-2-3-years - a genuinely fast-growing, high-ROE, debt-light micro-cap with a distribution/design moat, a formalising end-market and a cheap ~10x multiple; classification stays unconfirmed because persistent negative operating cash flow, H2 FY26 deceleration and SME scale make a literal near-term 10x a stretch - treat it as a multi-year rather than 2-3-year multibagger case, contingent on cash flow turning
verdict_headline: High-ROE, debt-light garden-decor micro-cap - FY26 confirmed ~22% growth, ~29% EBITDA margin and a cheap 10x multiple, but also negative operating cash flow before capex and H2 deceleration. Conviction Medium, unconfirmed
verdict_reasoning: Deep-dive pass 1 (FY26 filing + H1/H2 FY26 results + concall + BSE announcements). The trailing record (~25% ROE, ~25% 3-yr CAGR, near-zero debt) and FY26 actuals (revenue Rs 68.7 Cr +22%, PAT Rs 12.5 Cr +29%, EBITDA Rs 19.8 Cr ~29% margin, ROE 23.3%, net worth +44%) are strong, and the end-market (urban gardening, landscaping, hospitality/infra decor) is formalising.

The FY26 filing turned the cash-flow concern from hypothetical to evidenced: operating cash flow was negative Rs 8.4 Cr BEFORE capex of Rs 8.5 Cr, and ~Rs 3.8 Cr of new secured loans were drawn to bridge the gap. H2 FY26 growth also decelerated sharply (revenue +15% vs H1 ~+31-35%). Against that, the stock is genuinely cheap at ~10x FY26 earnings / ~6.5x EV/EBITDA, so the market is already discounting these risks.
